July 14, 1972
133
Mr. G. Douglas Hofe, Jr. Director Bureau of Outdoor Recreation U.S. Department of the Interior Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Mr. Hofe:
The draft environmental impact statement for "Departmental Implementation of Executive Order 11644 Pertaining to Use of Off-Road Vehicles on the Public Lands" which accompanied your letter of June 1, 1972, has been received by the Department of Commerce for review and comment.
The Department of Commerce has reviewed the draft environmental statement and has the following comments to offer for your consideration.
Summary Paragraph 2 line 4 - We suggest that you amend the sentence that begins "The directive establishes policies..." to read "The memorandum . . ."
Page 12 line 3 and 4 - In stating "Further, many resource interests will be affected" the implication derived is one of wide ranging affects. We suggest that you delineate those resources affected and to what degree of affectation this directive will have. We would call your attention to 16 USC 478 which provides for access to public lands for the purpose of prospecting. The restriction of ORV's to designated areas could not apply in this case. However, environmental, health and safety concerns should be made available to the prospector.
We hope these comments will be helpful to you in the preparation of the final statement.
Sincerely,
Sidney P. Galler
Deputy Assistant Secretary for Environmental Affairs
